title: Jeffrey M. Black v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied remand, ruled the newly raised procedural objection administratively out of order, and held that Presbytery did not err in treating the licentiate’s non-Calendar-Day view as no exception to the Westminster Standards.
first_summary: Black challenged Presbytery’s handling of his complaint and its ruling that a licentiate’s non-24-hour creation-day view was not an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC denied remand, treated Presbytery’s failed motions as an effective denial, and found no constitutional requirement that Black be present. It also upheld Presbytery’s ruling because the Standards did not require every non-Calendar-Day view to be recorded as an exception.
summary: Black challenged Presbytery’s handling of his complaint and its ruling that a licentiate’s non-24-hour creation-day view was not an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC denied remand because Presbytery had effectively adjudicated the complaint; the separate objection to proceeding without Black was not first filed below and was administratively out of order. It upheld Presbytery’s ruling that not every non-Calendar-Day view constitutes an exception. Because the record did not identify the licentiate’s precise view, the decision did not determine its acceptability or whether it could be taught.
